headline: Amazon Prime Air expands drone delivery to nearly 500 US cities and towns
summary: Amazon Prime Air, the company's drone delivery service, is significantly expanding its reach, aiming to serve nearly 500 US cities and towns.
details: Amazon Prime Air, the company's drone delivery service, has announced a significant expansion of its availability. This move aims to bring drone deliveries to nearly 500 cities and towns across the US.

The expansion marks a major step in Amazon's efforts to integrate autonomous delivery into its logistics network. It promises faster delivery options for eligible items to customers in these new service areas.

headline: CareCloud confirms 3.7M patients had their medical records stolen in data breach
summary: Health data giant CareCloud has confirmed a data breach affecting over 3.75 million patients, making it the fifth-largest health data theft of 2026 to date.
details: Hackers have stolen the personal information and medical records of more than 3.75 million people in a data breach at health data giant CareCloud. This disclosure marks the first confirmation of the scale of the incident, which is now the fifth-largest theft of health data in 2026 so far.

CareCloud detailed the March data breach in a filing with the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The number of affected victims was reportedly revised up in an update, though it's unclear if the figure is expected to rise further.

The New Jersey-based tech company provides electronic medical record storage to tens of thousands of healthcare providers across the United States. CareCloud handles a large amount of patient data and billing information on behalf of hospitals, doctor’s offices, and other medical practices.

The company previously stated hackers accessed patients’ medical data stored in one of its cloud storage environments over six days in March. Later notifications confirmed that data was exfiltrated from CareCloud's Amazon Web Services account.

The stolen data is extensive, including patients’ names, postal addresses, Social Security numbers, and their medical and health information. Government-issued identification numbers, such as passports and driver’s licenses, as well as banking and financial information, were also compromised.

CareCloud chief executive Stephen Snyder has not responded to multiple emails requesting information about the incident. Questions remain regarding whether the company paid hackers, who is responsible for cybersecurity, or if Snyder plans to resign.

This breach follows several other significant healthcare data incidents confirmed this year. Tech giant TriZetto reported a 2024 breach affecting 3.4 million people, and healthtech billing software maker Craneware experienced a July breach impacting an unspecified number of individuals.

According to HHS’ running tally, dental insurance giant DentaQuest currently holds the record for the largest data breach this year. Their incident affected at least 15 million people’s personal and health information.
